in_scope: in-code observability hooks only (production monitoring infra N/A for local foundation story)

findings.description: BR-09 call-boundary logging is fully implemented in lib/ai/claude.ts. The log() function emits: requestId, promptName, model, ok (boolean), and reason (on failure). All four required fields are present (requestId + promptName + model + validation outcome).

PII audit passed. The log() function is explicitly documented 'never logs raw model text or PII'. It only logs metadata fields (requestId, promptName, model, ok, reason). The variables/parsed data payload is never passed to log(). No real names or emails are in scope — seed data uses synthetic handles and @vertex.test domains.

No secrets in logs. The log entry does not include API keys, tokens, or any environment variable values. The ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and other secrets are read from env vars and never flow into the log call.

Production monitoring infra (dashboards, alert rules, runbooks, Prometheus/Application Insights instrumentation) does not exist. This is expected and correct for a LOCAL-ONLY foundation/data-infra story with no deployed service surface.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging, RED metrics, and alerting configuration in a future deployment story (SKILL-2+) when the Next.js API routes and live Anthropic SDK calls are wired up.

findings.description: console.debug is used as the logging sink. For a local hackathon story this is acceptable, but a structured logger (e.g. pino) with severity levels and JSON output would improve diagnosability once the service is deployed.
findings.recommendation: Replace console.debug with a structured logger in the deployment-ready story.
